title: Fix the double-counting set by wrapping it

task.text: `HashSet.addAll` calls `add` internally, so the subclass counts twice, and patching the arithmetic would break on the next JDK. Stop inheriting the implementation: wrap a `Set` and forward to it.

items: `added()` counts every element offered through `add` or `addAll`, duplicates included.
`CountingSet<E>` is still a `Set<E>` with a no-arg constructor, and no longer extends `HashSet`.
Add `CountingSet(Set<E> inner)`; all storage, ordering and equality come from `inner`.

checks.title: It still behaves as a Set
CountingSet wraps any Set it is given

hints.text: The bug lives in `HashSet`, which calls `add` from `addAll`. A subclass depends on that private detail. Hold a set instead of being one.
Keep a `private final Set<E> inner`. Count in `add`, make `addAll` loop over its argument calling your own `add`, and forward everything else. Extending `AbstractSet` saves most of the boilerplate.

lines: @Override public boolean add(E e) { added++; return inner.add(e); }
